cli.help: Remux mode imports audio tracks and subtitles from MKV files in different languages.
Split mode cuts MKV files into segments or episodes.
Metadata mode applies a metadata preset to MKV files.
--lang en|it                  CLI/UI language for this run
-ext, --extensions <list>      File extensions to scan. Default: mkv
-t,   --target-language <code> ISO 639-2 language code(s), e.g. ita or eng,ita
-l,   --language <path>        Folder with MKV files to import tracks from
If omitted, the source folder is used
-fs,  --framesync              Visual frame comparison for constant delay
-da,  --deep-analysis          dHash pipeline; imported audio requires format and lang/all scope
--speed-correction <m>   off or manual; materializes audio stretch with FFmpeg
--subtitle-canvas-rewrite Rewrite imported PGS, ASS/SSA, VobSub geometry
--audio-format <fmt>     flac, lpcm, aac, opus, ac3; required for Speed/Deep audio
--audio-scope <scope>    disabled, lang, all; Speed/Deep require lang or all
--output-template <tpl>   Output name template, no extension ({{source}} {{n}} {{episode}} {{chapter}} {{start}} {{end}} {{duration}}, padding :02)
--chapters-per-episode <k>  Group chapters into blocks of k
--snap off|before|after|nearest  (default: nearest, aligns to keyframe and avoids re-encoding)
Common: ita, eng, jpn, ger/deu, fra/fre, spa, por, rus, chi/zho, kor

web.config.help.split.source.title: Source
web.config.help.split.source.text: Required. Select a single MKV file or a folder. With a folder, the scan prepares a batch using the same options for all MKV files found.
web.config.help.split.output.title: Output
web.config.help.split.output.text: Optional. Must be a folder. If it remains empty, each output is written to the input file folder.
web.config.help.split.recursive.title: Recursive
web.config.help.split.recursive.text: Used only when Source is a folder. Includes MKV files in subfolders during the scan.
web.config.help.split.force.title: Force
web.config.help.split.force.text: If enabled, overwrites existing outputs. If disabled, segments that already exist are skipped.
web.config.help.split.mode.title: Mode
web.config.help.split.mode.text: Required. Cut modes are alternatives: choose only one. Form fields change based on the selected mode.
web.config.help.split.pattern.title: Pattern
web.config.help.split.pattern.text: Required in Chapter pattern mode. Example: 5,5,5,6. The sum must match the number of chapters in the file. Naming is managed only with Template.
web.config.help.split.ranges.title: Ranges
web.config.help.split.ranges.text: Required in Ranges mode. Explicit intervals separated by comma. Example: 00:00:00-00:21:40,00:21:40-END.
web.config.help.split.splitAt.title: Split at
web.config.help.split.splitAt.text: Required in Split at mode. List of cut points; generates N+1 segments. Example: 20:00,40:00.
web.config.help.split.trimStart.title: Trim start
web.config.help.split.trimStart.text: In Trim mode, drops everything before this point. Can be filled together with Trim end.
web.config.help.split.trimEnd.title: Trim end
web.config.help.split.trimEnd.text: In Trim mode, drops everything after this point. Can be filled together with Trim start.
web.config.help.split.snap.title: Snap
web.config.help.split.snap.text: The cut aligns to the chosen keyframe: direct copy, no re-encode. "Frame exact" cuts where you ask but re-encodes the leading GOP of every segment, which costs hours. The boundary between two adjacent segments moves as one, so partitioning neither loses nor duplicates frames.
web.config.help.split.extensions.title: Extensions
web.config.help.split.template.title: Template
web.config.help.split.template.text: Optional. When empty the mode default is used, and the field pre-fills with it.
The .mkv extension is added by the program: do not write it in the template.
Slashes create subfolders under the output folder.
episode number, starts at the "start numbering at" value
name of the segment's first chapter
zero-pad to two digits, the only format allowed
web.config.help.remux.source.title: Source
web.config.help.remux.source.text: Folder with source MKV files. Remux works by episode scan/matching.
web.config.help.remux.language.title: Language
web.config.help.remux.language.text: Folder with MKV files to import audio/subtitle tracks from. If empty, uses Source also as the language folder.
web.config.help.remux.destination.title: Destination
web.config.help.remux.destination.text: Output folder. As an alternative, Overwrite source can be used.
web.config.help.remux.overwrite.title: Overwrite source
web.config.help.remux.overwrite.text: Writes the result in place of the source file. Alternative to the Destination folder.
web.config.help.remux.recursive.title: Recursive
web.config.help.remux.target.title: Target language
web.config.help.remux.target.text: Languages of audio/subtitle tracks to import from the Language file.
Accepts three-letter ISO 639-2 codes recognized by MKV metadata.
web.config.help.remux.audioCodec.title: Audio codec
web.config.help.remux.audioCodec.text: Optional filter on audio codecs to import from the Language file. Empty = imports all audio codecs of the target language.
Format: codecs or aliases separated by comma.
DTS matches only the DTS core, not DTS-HD MA.
DTS-HD matches DTS-HD MA and DTS-HD HR.
web.config.help.remux.keepAudio.title: Keep audio
web.config.help.remux.keepAudio.text: Audio languages to keep from the original Source. Empty = keeps all source audio tracks that are not replaced by the imported language.
Accepts three-letter ISO 639-2 codes recognized by MKV metadata.
web.config.help.remux.keepCodec.title: Keep codec
web.config.help.remux.keepCodec.text: Optional filter on audio codecs to keep from the original Source. Empty = no codec filter on kept source audio tracks.
Format: codecs or aliases separated by comma.
DTS matches only the DTS core, not DTS-HD MA.
DTS-HD matches DTS-HD MA and DTS-HD HR.
web.config.help.remux.keepSub.title: Keep sub
web.config.help.remux.keepSub.text: Subtitle languages to keep from the original Source. Empty = keeps all source subtitles.
Accepts three-letter ISO 639-2 codes recognized by MKV metadata.
web.config.help.remux.subOnly.title: Subtitles only
web.config.help.remux.subOnly.text: Imports only subtitles from the language file, ignoring audio.
web.config.help.remux.audioOnly.title: Audio only
web.config.help.remux.audioOnly.text: Imports only audio from the language file, ignoring subtitles.
web.config.help.remux.speed.title: Speed
web.config.help.remux.speed.text: Speed correction through temporal stretch. Language audio tracks are rendered by FFmpeg in the selected format; video is not re-encoded.
Select the known Source and Language playback rates. The factor is verified visually and the initial delay is resolved automatically.
web.config.help.remux.framesync.title: Frame-sync
web.config.help.remux.framesync.text: Calculates a fixed offset from audio correlation or dHash voting, and verifies it in distributed checkpoints. Does not fix edits/cuts in the middle.
web.config.help.remux.deep.title: Deep analysis
web.config.help.remux.deep.text: Full analysis for releases with added/removed scenes. Mutually exclusive with Frame-sync.
When audio is imported, it requires an Audio format up front and processes every Language track in the batch, even when an episode produces no cut/insert operations.
web.config.help.remux.cropSource.title: Crop src
web.config.help.remux.cropSource.text: Manual crop applied only to Source frames used for visual matching.
Format: L:R:T:B in pixels on the original frame before scaling. Empty or 0:0:0:0 keeps automatic border detection enabled; a non-zero value overrides it. Does not crop the final output.
web.config.help.remux.cropLang.title: Crop lang
web.config.help.remux.cropLang.text: Manual crop applied only to Language frames used for visual matching.
Format: L:R:T:B in pixels on the original frame before scaling. Empty or 0:0:0:0 keeps automatic border detection enabled; a non-zero value overrides it. Does not crop the final output.
web.config.help.remux.subCanvas.title: Sub canvas
web.config.help.remux.subCanvas.text: Optional. Rewrites canvas and coordinates for imported subtitles when resolution, display area or crop differs.
Applies to PGS, ASS/SSA and VobSub when analysis geometry makes the transformation safe.
web.config.help.remux.audioDelay.title: Audio delay
web.config.help.remux.audioDelay.text: Manual offset in milliseconds added to the automatic synchronization result.
web.config.help.remux.subDelay.title: Sub delay
web.config.help.remux.subDelay.text: Manual offset in milliseconds added to the automatic synchronization result for imported subtitles.
web.config.help.remux.audioSourceFill.te: Enables filling missing parts using an audio track already present in the Source.
Appears only after choosing an Audio format. When enabled, it requires Threshold, Source language, at least one mode, and Audio set to Lang or All.
web.config.help.remux.audioSourceFillThr: Required with Audio source fill enabled. When an enabled condition exceeds this threshold, RemuxForge takes that specific audio segment from the Source and concatenates it to the track imported from the Language file.
web.config.help.remux.audioSourceFillLan: Language of the Source audio track to take fill segments from. Required with Audio source fill enabled.
Accepts three-letter ISO 639-2 codes recognized by MKV metadata.
web.config.help.remux.audioSourceFillSta: Applies filling at the beginning of the file.
If the positive initial audio delay exceeds the Audio source fill threshold, RemuxForge takes the first N milliseconds from the Source and prepends them to the track imported from the Language file.
Imported subtitles are not concatenated: they keep the calculated delay.
web.config.help.remux.audioSourceFillEnd: Applies filling at the end of the audio track.
The condition is: Source video duration - (rendered Language timeline duration + applied delay) > threshold.
The Source video timeline is always authoritative. If the selected Source audio ends earlier, the uncovered tail is padded with silence so the final duration remains exact.
web.config.help.remux.audioSourceFillIns: If the automatic or manually edited EditMap contains an INSERT_SILENCE operation greater than the Audio source fill threshold, RemuxForge does not insert silence: it takes the corresponding audio segment from the Source and concatenates it to the imported track.
web.config.help.remux.match.title: Pattern match
web.config.help.remux.match.text: Regex used to match episodes between Source and Language. Captured groups form the episode ID: two files match when they produce the same ID.
web.config.help.remux.extensions.title: Extensions
web.config.help.remux.extensions.text: Extensions searched during scan. Default: mkv. Multiple values separated by comma.
web.config.help.remux.audioFormat.title: Audio format
web.config.help.remux.audioFormat.text: Final format for processed audio tracks: FLAC, LPCM, AAC, Opus or AC-3.
Determines the codec of produced audio files. It is required for Audio source fill and when Speed Correction or Deep Analysis import Language audio.
web.config.help.remux.audioScope.title: Audio
web.config.help.remux.audioScope.text: Language processes every audio track imported from the language file. All extends the same processing to final Source tracks.
With Speed Correction, Deep Analysis or Audio source fill the minimum scope is Language: timeline corrections are not optional conversions.
web.config.help.remux.audio24.title: 24bit -> 16bit
web.config.help.remux.audio24.text: Forces processed audio track output to 16-bit, using soxr VHQ and Shibata dither when conversion is needed. Available only for FLAC and LPCM.
web.config.help.remux.audioNormalize.tex: Global multichannel peak normalization. The allowed target range is -60 to 0 dB.
web.config.help.remux.encoding.title: Video encoding
web.config.help.remux.encoding.text: Optional post-merge video re-encoding profile. Profiles are managed from Settings > Encoding profiles.

web.metadata.presetDialog.help.default.t: Define IF/THEN rules evaluated in order. Each rule works on the result produced by previous rules.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.preset.te: Select a preset saved in the RemuxForge configuration folder or create a new one. The path is not selected manually.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.presetNam: Name used to save the JSON file in the RemuxForge preset folder. It is not part of the pipeline applied to files.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.ruleDescr: Required field. It should describe what the rule does because it is the readable identifier in the pipeline.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.ruleEnabl: Temporarily disables the rule without deleting it from the preset.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.advancedF: Shows less common editable fields that are still allowed. Dangerous fields remain excluded.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.scope.tex: Chooses where the rule is applied: Matroska container, video tracks, audio tracks, or subtitle tracks. Conditions and editable fields depend on this value.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.condition: Field read from the current pipeline state. After actions run, later rules see updated values; conditions in the same rule are evaluated before its actions.
Comparison applied to the selected field: equality, contains, regex, range, presence, or numeric comparison.
Literal value or template. You can insert tokens from the browser, for example [audio_language], [video_width], or function expressions.
Unit used to normalize numeric comparisons, sizes, and durations.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.trackComp: Compares the current track field with other tracks in the selected group, for example largest or rank 1.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.trackGrou: Defines which other tracks participate in the comparison: same language, same format, same type, or equivalent combinations.
Counts tracks in the selected group and compares that number with the entered value.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.operation: Chooses the action run when conditions are true: set or clear fields and tags, manage statistics tags, set exclusive flags, or remove a track.
Editable field for the action scope. Set and Clear always act on the field selected from this list.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.exclusive: When setting an exclusive flag, other tracks in the same group are updated consistently.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.operation: Template applied to the selected field. Supports tokens like [file_stem] and functions like {[file_name]:TrimEnd(4)}.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.tagTarget: Current follows the rule scope; File applies the tag to the container; Current track applies it to the evaluated track; All tracks applies it to every track not removed.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.tagKey.te: Tag key selectable from the UI. Free XML is not available.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.clearTags: Requires explicit confirmation before clearing managed tags. A new operation uses the current rule target; an imported preset can specify File, Current track, or All tracks.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.attachmen: Name the attachment takes inside the MKV. Leave it empty when attaching a file and the source file name is used. The cover convention is cover.jpg or cover.png.
Path of the file to attach. It may contain expressions, so the cover can differ per file.
MIME type of the attachment. Leave it empty to derive it from the name extension.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.chapterPa: Name given to every chapter. {n} is the number, {n:02} the two-digit number, {name} the current name. Chapters are rewritten as a block, but positions are left alone: only names are governed here.
web.metadata.presetDialog.help.trackOrde: Order in which to write track types, comma separated. Careful: reordering tracks forces a full mkvmerge remux, so the cost goes from seconds to minutes per file.
Languages in priority order within each type, comma separated, for example ita,eng,jpn. Languages not listed go last, and tracks with the same type and language keep the file order.
What the tag refers to: 50 the episode or movie, 60 the season, 70 the series. Matroska has no tags named SEASON or EPISODE: the season is PART_NUMBER at level 60 and the episode is PART_NUMBER at level 50. When missing, the level is 50.

web.metadata.help.readOnly: It is available to conditions and tokens but cannot be changed.
web.metadata.help.clearable: It can be set or cleared.
web.metadata.help.notClearable: It can be set but not cleared.

web.config.modeNote.chapters-per-episode: Groups chapters into blocks of k, adapting to each file's count. Partitions the source: nothing is discarded.
web.config.modeNote.pattern: Groups chapters following the list you write, which must add up to that file's chapters. Partitions the source: nothing is discarded.
web.config.modeNote.chapters-each: One output file per chapter. Partitions the source: nothing is discarded.
web.config.modeNote.split-at: Cuts the file at the given points. One point yields two files, two points yield three: nothing is discarded.
web.config.modeNote.ranges: Produces one file per listed range. Everything outside the ranges is discarded.
web.config.modeNote.trim: Produces a single file, dropping the given head and tail. The trimmed material is discarded.
web.config.modeNote.manual: No cut comes from the configuration: segments are drawn in the editor, file by file, on the timeline.
web.config.validation.chaptersPerEpisode: Chapters per episode: must be at least 1
web.config.help.split.chaptersPerEpisode: How many chapters make one episode. It adapts to any count, so a folder of discs with different chapter counts no longer fails file by file. With 1 it produces one file per chapter. When the division is not exact the last episode is shorter and the plan says so.
